question: Is a gene's presence in annotation databases predictable from its measurable properties (expression, length, protein class)? If yes, enrichment conclusions drawn from annotated subsets are vulnerable to selection-on-observability; test whether headline conclusions survive inverse-probability weighting.
universe: the 18,399-gene propensity pool from Tier-1 #2 (genes with GTEx median TPM + HPA protein class + MyGene length), rebuilt deterministically from committed sources

missingness_outcomes.in_hpa_protein: gene present in HPA proteinatlas.tsv (20,163 genes) - protein-level annotation exists
missingness_outcomes.has_subcellular: gene present in data/subcellular_location.tsv (13,148 genes) - subcellular localization annotated
missingness_outcomes.has_uniprot_membrane: gene present in data/uniprot_cellmembrane.tsv (4,124 genes) - membrane annotation exists
missingness_outcomes.gtex_expressed: GTEx v8 median TPM >= 1 in at least 25% of tissues - reliably RNA-detectable

model: logistic regression (L2, sklearn LogisticRegression max_iter=2000) per outcome on the 7 locked propensity features, 5-fold CV AUC (KFold shuffle seed 20260929) reported per outcome; a model with CV AUC <= 0.6 is reported as weakly informative
endpoints: CV AUC per missingness outcome (is observability predictable at all?)
candidate vs pool P(observation): median predicted observability of the 96 gated candidates vs pool median, per outcome - quantifies selection-on-observability

conclusion survival: candidate-vs-matched-control contrasts (publication_count, generif_count medians from #2/#3) recomputed with inverse-probability-of-observation weights (IPW, weights trimmed at 1st/99th percentile); pre-declared survival rule: conclusion survives if the IPW contrast keeps the sign of the unweighted contrast and retains >= 50% of its magnitude
interpretation_rule: if observability is predictable (AUC > 0.6) AND candidates sit far above pool median P(obs), selection-on-observability is real and reported as a structural limitation; the IPW survival numbers then state how much of each headline contrast is robust to it. All directions reported as measured.
known_gap: database presence is measured on locally committed snapshots; a gene absent from a snapshot may be absent for curation reasons unrelated to its properties. Pharos per-gene outcomes remain non-genome-wide (gap from #2/#3).
